You audit phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER. Today is Thursday, September 24, 2026, 4:40 PM (local time).
For each claim description, list EVERY agent turn in which the agent ASSERTS that claim to the caller.
- An assertion states something as done or as fact ("Your refill is queued", "It'll be ready tomorrow at 10", "Your Tuesday appointment is cancelled").
- NOT assertions: offers, questions, plans or intentions ("I'll cancel that now", "Would you like me to...", "Let me check"), or statements that it could NOT be done.
- Judge only what the agent said. Do not decide whether the claim is true.
- Cite the turn number shown as [#N].
- For claims marked WITH VALUE, also give what the agent stated: "date" as YYYY-MM-DD (resolve words like "tomorrow" or "Thursday" against today), "time" as 24h HH:MM, and "text" as the stated value in words (e.g. an address). Use null for parts not stated.
Reply with JSON only: {"<claim id>": [{"turn": N, "quote": "<short exact quote>", "date": ..., "time": ..., "text": ...}], ...}. Use [] when the claim is never made.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi honey, Tess Morgan. Dr. Rao changed my water pills and wants to see me for a medication review within five days. What do you have?
[#4] AGENT: Hi Tess! I'd be happy to help you find a medication review appointment with Dr. Rao within the next five days. Let me check what's available. Unfortunately, Dr. Rao doesn't have any medication review slots open in the next five days. Would you like me to add you to the waitlist for Dr. Rao, or would you be open to seeing another provider sooner?
CALLER: Can't you squeeze me in, honey? She said five days, and it's important since she changed my water pills.
[#9] AGENT: I understand this is important, Tess. Let me check if there are any same-day sick appointments or other visit types that might work, and I'll also look at the next week to see what Dr. Rao has available. Dr. Rao doesn't have any med review slots available through early October. What I can do is put you on the waitlist for Dr. Rao so you're first in line if something opens up, and we can also flag a callback so the clinic reaches out to you about getting you in. Would that work for you?
CALLER: Okay, put me on the list, honey. But don't let it slip through the cracks, alright?
[#12] AGENT: I'd be happy to add you to the waitlist for Dr. Rao. Before I do, I need to verify your identity—can you give me your date of birth?
CALLER: Okay, that's fine, honey. January 19th, 1974.
[#21] AGENT: Thank you. Now let me add you to the waitlist for Dr. Rao and flag a callback so the clinic makes sure to reach out to you. Perfect, Tess. You're on the waitlist for Dr. Rao for a medication review through September 29th, and I've flagged a callback so the clinic will reach out to you. They'll make sure this doesn't slip through the cracks.
CALLER: Alright honey, thank you for taking care of that. Bye now.

A06.claim.2: Agent says she is on the waitlist.
A06.claim.3: Agent says Dr. Rao's team will call her.
